title: Can every course be finished?
summary: Start with the courses that need nothing, then unlock the courses waiting on them; if some never unlock, there is a loop.
goal: Decide whether all the courses can be completed

examples.label: A loop
examples.explanation: Each course needs the other first.

ladder.name: Scan repeatedly for a course you can take
ladder.idea: Repeatedly scan all courses for one whose prerequisites are all done, take it, and start the scan again.

ladder.name: Unlock courses with a queue
ladder.idea: Count each course's missing prerequisites. Queue every course with none. Taking a course lowers the count of courses that need it; any count reaching zero joins the queue.
ladder.insight: Taking a course can only unlock the courses that list it as a prerequisite. Keeping counts means each prerequisite is checked once instead of rescanning everything.

transfer.problem: A build system compiles modules that depend on other modules. Decide whether a valid build order exists.
transfer.explanation: Modules are nodes and dependencies edges; repeatedly build modules with no unbuilt dependencies, and fail if some never become ready.

selfCheck: Counts missing prerequisites (in-degrees) for every course.
Starts the queue with all courses that need nothing.
Lowers counts only of courses that depend on the one taken.
Returns whether every course was taken.
